source_preflight.notes: Director finding 1 (tradition-wide naming): the opening now reads 'what William Benham calls this line in his classical Western text' instead of 'actually called in the classical Western tradition' — narrowed to the single verified author, no tradition-wide consensus implied. Director finding 2 (prevalence/universality): 'Not every hand carries a Via Lascivia. As with the other minor lines... its absence is not a gap' was removed entirely (it was unattributed, site-wide framing, not sourced to Benham); the retained sentence attributes the chance-line/fixed-minor-line distinction directly and explicitly to Benham and states it is 'not a modern prevalence claim about hands today,' matching the evidence note's 'without converting that into a modern frequency claim' instruction. Director finding 3 (comparative-strength phrase): 'could just as easily be expressed' was changed to 'could be expressed' in both the body section and the parallel FAQ answer, matching the evidence note's 'could express the same surplus energy in other activity instead' (no comparative claim). Full-article re-check beyond the three named sentences: no other prevalence/consensus/frequency wording found; every historical/interpretive claim (course, sister-line relationship, chance-line classification, historical name/surplus-energy reading, non-sensual-hand qualification) is attributed specifically to Benham and matches the evidence note's safe boundary; the 'in context' section explicitly declines to extend the Mercury line's own health/vitality/business associations onto the Via Lascivia, so no new combination reading was introduced; no anonymous authority phrasing ('modern palmists', 'some writers', 'experts') appears anywhere; no quotation marks are used around any Benham content (all paraphrased) — the only quoted string is 'allergy line', used strictly as a labeled search term per the evidence note's instruction; the historical-name section and the allergy-line/medical-safety section remain visibly separate; no medical, legal, financial, deterministic-relationship, criminality, or predictive-science claim is introduced anywhere in the article.
